main_concepts.simple_explanation: HTML supports Ordered Lists (`<ol>`) for numbered items (1, 2, 3) and Unordered Lists (`<ul>`) for bullet points. Inside both, we use `<li>` (List Item) to add the actual points.
To add an image, use the empty tag `` with the `src` attribute (e.g., ``). To create a clickable link, use the anchor tag `` with the `href` attribute (e.g., `Click Here`).
Tables are created using `<table>`. Rows are defined by `<tr>`. Table Headings use `<th>` (bold and centered), and regular table data cells use `<td>`.
Forms let users input data. The `<form>` tag wraps elements like text boxes (`<input type="text">`), radio buttons for single choices, checkboxes for multiple choices, and a submit button.

fun_activity.title: 🔗 The Infinite Web
fun_activity.instructions: Create a file named 'page1.html' and another named 'page2.html'. Put a link in page 1 that goes to page 2, and a link in page 2 that goes back to page 1. You just created your own mini-internet loop!

exam_tips: 📌 The `alt` attribute in the `` tag is crucial! It provides alternative text if the image fails to load and helps screen readers for visually impaired users.
📌 `colspan` merges columns horizontally (left to right), while `rowspan` merges rows vertically (top to bottom).
📌 Radio buttons (`type="radio"`) allow selecting only ONE option, while Checkboxes (`type="checkbox"`) allow selecting MULTIPLE options.
quick_recap: ⭐ The `<a>` tag stands for Anchor tag and is used to create hyperlinks.
⭐ The `type` attribute in `<ol>` can change numbers to Roman numerals (I, ii) or alphabets (A, a).
⭐ A web form sends user input to a server for processing.
